title: Working on a Valheim-like game for mobile
author: nospoon99
selftext:
After experimenting with techniques for a while I decided to try creating something I really want and couldn't find: a simple game like Valheim for mobile. I'm a big fan of the game, played it in very early access and with the recent release of 1.0 it triggered me to start working on this project.

This time, I did the exact opposite of my previous experiments: instead of working on the look I cut corners using existing assets and used low poly, then focused on the gameplay. My challenge was to create a game I would actually want to play on my phone.

Working this way has been extremely enjoyable, I was able to focus on the things that AI can't do: is the game fun? Is the progression interesting? Is the balance ok? Working on optimisations too to keep it running at 60fps on my 4 year old phone. I also chose ancient Gaul (France) as a theme and I'm loving learning about their gods and picking references.

I have 2 biome ready, full with different zones, animals, loot, materials and monsters (and 2 bosses). Around 3 to 4 hours of solid gameplay so far.

This is gearing up to be a simplified take on Valheim suitable for mobile: challenging but less grind, more permissive storage, simplified build etc... 



**Now, for the workflow:** 

\- Opus 5.5

\- Godot MCP with C#: pretty much everything in the game is data, so it's easier for LLMs to work with a more widely used language for this.

\- Blender MCP

\- Starting with existing assets (good old KayKit) instead of starting from scratch: I have found this to save me a tone of time. AI still struggle with animations, so starting with an asset close to what I want and get Opus to amend got me decent result more quickly.

\- I started with stock assets then started to amend more and more as I went

\- For look and feel I start with real reference images, experiment with gen AI image tools to get something I like then give it to Opus to replicate



Opus 5.5 has been amazing to work with. Usage has been great on Max 5 plan, not sure how much tokens I used so far but I'm not reaching my 5h windows working normally (plan, implement, review, test iterate etc...)

Planning to make it available for free on Google Play for early access. If some want to try it hit me up.
